title: Assessing the Effect of Infant-directed Unidirectional Feeding Valves on Milk Volume Intake in Infants With Cleft Palate
official: Assessing the Effect of Infant-directed Unidirectional Feeding Valves on Milk Volume Intake in Infants With Cleft Palate- A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: This study aims to assess the impact of using a cleft-adapted bottle with a unidirectional valve compared with a non-cleft-adapted bottle on oral volume intake and milk transfer rate.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Infants with a diagnosed, unrepaired, overt cleft palate under 12 months gestational age cared for at Phoenix Children's, upon receipt of parental/guardian informed consent to participate.
* Infant is using the Dr. Brown's® Zero-Resistance Specialty Feeding System® (Narrow nipple or wide-neck options) or the Pigeon Baby Cleft Palate Bottle
* Infants feeding using milk at IDDSI level 0 (expressed breast milk, commercial formulas, and formula fortified up to 26kcal/ounce)

Exclusion Criteria:

* Infants with a submucous cleft palate.
* Infants receiving supplemental enteral (e.g. "tube") feedings.
* Infants receiving thickened feeds with infant cereal (oatmeal or rice), Gelmix, or pureed food
